executive_summary: A coupon dominated by Championship mid-week congestion and Premier League fatigue signals. Four games earn single-worthy confidence: Arsenal at home despite Saka's absence, Southampton's visit to a hapless Preston, West Ham's superb away record carrying them past Blackburn, and Middlesbrough's league-leader quality overpowering Watford despite tight turnaround. The Championship batch is defined by an extraordinary injury burden on Millwall and Newcastle, which opens clear value on West Brom and Fulham respectively. The two FA Cup ties — Crewe vs Wimbledon and Oxford vs Stevenage — are genuinely low-data environments where confidence is capped, and the Cardiff vs Burnley defensive crisis makes that match a genuine toss-up.
value_radar: Game 3 (Fulham vs Newcastle): Newcastle are missing Joelinton, Ramsey (suspended), Livramento, and Jaouen, with Miley only 50-50. That is roughly half a first XI gone. At 2.23 Fulham are undervalued — Fulham's xGF has also been systematically underperforming by 0.70 per game across the last five matches, suggesting a correction is due.

Game 11 (West Brom vs Millwall): Millwall are reported to have five senior players out including two midfielders and two defenders, their away record reads W2 D1 L4, and West Brom's last-five xGF of 2.46 — the highest of any team on the coupon — is barely being reflected in their actual goals. Odds of 2.14 for West Brom at home look loose.

Game 10 (Watford vs Middlesbrough): Boro at 1.52 looks short on the surface, but their xGF/g of 2.06 and xPts of 29 vs actual 28 show their position is entirely deserved and not built on luck. Watford's xGA of 1.75 against a team averaging over 2.0 xGF is a mismatch. Even with 2d rest and rotation, Boro's depth in this Championship is superior.

Arteta's side have also beaten Lille and hammered Leeds at the Emirates, underscoring a fortress mentality on home soil. The xGF underperformance of -0.19 across the last five matches is negligible — this is a team whose quality is genuine and whose xPts of 18 against actual 24 tells you they have converted chances efficiently, though there is a mild regression note to monitor over time. The critical missing piece is Bukayo Saka, confirmed out for several weeks and not simply doubtful. Saka accounted for 3G/0A and was Arsenal's set-piece taker — his absence removes a creative hub on the right and will force Arteta to reshuffle. Dowman is also suspended until late November, adding a second confirmed absence. These are real costs, not trivial squad attrition.

Jakirovic's ability to put out a coherent, balanced XI for a trip to the Emirates is severely compromised.

The tactical picture is blunt: Hull will almost certainly sit deep, attempt to frustrate Arsenal's build-up, and hope for a set-piece or counter. Without Saka as the primary threat, there is a slight question about Arsenal finding the breakthrough early enough to relax. However, the depth of talent available to Arteta — Martinelli, Trossard, Odegaard, Havertz — means the absence of one player, however important, should not derail a home performance against Championship opposition.

This is about as close to a banker as you will find on the coupon. The 1.17 price is skinny and reflects genuine probability. Arsenal's home dominance, Hull's catastrophic injury list, and the quality chasm between the sides all point emphatically in one direction. The only credible risk is a historic cup-tie upset — but this is a league game, reducing that factor significantly.

The H2H is relevant and encouraging for the home side: Fulham beat Newcastle 2-0 at home last season, and have won three of the last four meetings at Craven Cottage across all competitions.
